## Where the agents sat on the DRC model

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- On [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] agents wrote the code. The model structure
  and approach were specified by me at a high level
- The judgements stayed with people
- Agents do best with something to check against. A simulation with
  known parameters, an analytic case, another group's estimate
- 333 of 425 pull requests, the unit of change on GitHub, came from my
  bot account

::: {.attribution}
[github.com/epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize][bvd], `README.md` · pull
request count from the GitHub API, 2026-09-11
:::
:::

## Agents building and checking the parts

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
- **Replication.** The McCabe et al. Imperial report replicated in a few
  hours, the day after it appeared. Then a joint model across five
  situation report streams, the Uganda exports and a genomic bound
- **Data.** Agents read the French PDF situation reports, two blind
  reads each. Onsets are only a figure, so an agent-written digitiser,
  cross-checked by a second one in another language
- **Checks on every rebuild.** Predictive checks per stream, forecasts
  scored against later data, the replication. That much debugging
  would not have happened by hand
- Infrastructure and review were still needed to keep the agents in
  check
- Could agents build and check the simulators you learn against?

::: {.attribution}
[BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] `README.md` and `data/README.md`, SitReps 104 to
114 · McCabe et al. report of 18 May 2026
:::
:::

## Agents that search over models {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **On the DRC model this was ad hoc.** Agents proposed patches as
  issues, one branch each. Every release was scored against later data
  and reviewed against domain knowledge
- **The systematic version, given a target, is a tree search.** Propose
  candidate models, fit and score, keep the best, branch again
- **Google did this for the 2025/26 CDC hubs.** A large language model
  (LLM) guided tree search that writes forecasting code. It matched or
  beat the hub ensembles for influenza, COVID-19 and respiratory
  syncytial virus (RSV), prospectively
- Bracher and Funk put the earlier claimed 11% retrospective gain down
  to data revisions leaking into the evaluation
- It mutates and composes models people built. The hubs, the data, the
  evaluation target and the review of output were still people's work

::: {.attribution}
Martinson, Brenner, Plomecka, Williams, Reich and Shamsi 2026,
[arXiv:2605.16238](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16238) · Bracher and Funk
2026, [arXiv:2608.05883](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.05883) ·
[BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] `README.md`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](../figures/exchange-tree-search.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A tree. The root is a task, forecast admissions, scored on
held-out weeks. Four proposed models below it: ARIMA and a GAM in grey,
dropped, and two renewal models in teal, kept. Under the kept ones four
more variants, adding a reporting delay, a spline, day of week effects
and a wastewater stream, with the spline dropped. Arrows from the
survivors lead to a red box, an ensemble of the survivors is what gets
submitted. Side labels read propose, write the code, fit, score, expand
the best, many rounds."}

::: {.attribution}
